chunks: He said: Ayyin ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayyin informed me that: Abdallah ibn Bakir sent me to Abdallah al-Kahili in the year of the taking of the Servant of God (peace be upon him) during the time of al-Mahdi, and said: Convey my greetings to him and ask him if the news has reached him... until he said: Convey greetings to him and tell him: Abu al-Izar narrated to me in your mosque thirty years ago, and he was saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The master of this affair will come to Iraq twice; as for the first time, his release will be hastened and his allowance will be improved, and as for the second time, he will be imprisoned so his imprisonment will be long, then he will be taken out from their hands by force.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The Servant of God (a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Affair (a title for Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What are the two predicted visits of Imam al-Mahdi to Iraq according to Imam al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the prophetic certainty of the Mahdi’s political trajectory, framing his imprisonment not as a defeat but as a divinely ordained phase preceding his ultimate emergence. The distinction between the first and second imprisonments underscores the gradual maturation of the Imam’s authority, a key theme in Shia eschatology regarding the transition from occultation to global justice.
